steps: Inspect first, no changes: fetch order O-3001 (get_order) and customer C-300. Record for every line: shipped/unshipped/backordered status, quantity, amount actually paid (after discounts), payment method, delivery date, any prior refunds, and whether stock was set aside. Confirm the order belongs to C-300.

Fetch the return policy (get_return_policy) and note the return window length and how a return is paid out once the window has closed (e.g. store credit vs original method). Compare today's date (2026-10-05) to the delivery/ship date of each shipped line to decide whether it is inside or outside the window.
Split the order into lines. Shipped lines go through the return path. Lines that never shipped are cancellations, not returns. Do not touch any other order, customer or product.

For unshipped lines: cancel them (cancel line/order tool) and refund each to the original card (refund_order with method=card) for what was paid for that line, never more. Restock the full quantity of each cancelled line that had stock set aside (restock tool). Skip restocking for backordered lines, which have no stock set aside. Do not change the shipping address of any shipped order.

For shipped lines: open the return (create/record return for those lines). Compute the refund per line as no more than the amount paid for it. If the line is inside the window, refund per the policy's in-window method (normally the original card). If it is outside the window, pay out exactly as the policy says (likely store credit).

Issue the refund(s) with refund_order using the policy-determined method and amounts. If any refund is store credit, also call apply_store_credit on C-300 for the same total amount, so it is both recorded on the order and added to the balance. Do not do one without the other.

Do NOT restock shipped/returned goods when the refund is issued. Restock them only when the warehouse has received them. Check the order or return record for a received status. If received, restock the returned quantities. If not, leave stock unchanged and note that restock is pending warehouse receipt, for example by marking the return as awaiting receipt.

Re-fetch O-3001 and C-300 to verify: line statuses, refund totals not above amounts paid, the store credit balance, and stock levels as expected. Then write a short summary for the customer and the record. It should state what was cancelled, what was returned, how each refund was paid, and what is pending warehouse receipt.

Shipped lines are returned, with the payout method set by the return window. So inspecting the order and the policy comes first. Refunds are capped at what was paid, store credit needs both records, and returns are restocked only on warehouse receipt. The plan also stays within O-3001 and leaves shipping addresses alone.

The window is measured from the date a line shipped, not from the order date.
A return requested more than 30 days after the line shipped must be paid out as store_credit, never back to the original payment method.
A line that never shipped is a cancellation, not a return: it is refunded to the original payment method (method=card) whatever the age of the order.
A refund for a line may never exceed the amount actually paid for that line.
Returned goods re-enter stock only once the warehouse receives them. Cancelled goods never left, so they are restocked immediately.
